comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

This is a [documented behavior](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/0e9d1f972a91acf5a0513319099ba41f7c09c30a/doc/mini-completion.txt#L103-L107): typing any non-keyword character will insert snippet (*if* its candidate is already selected). It is present for easier, more fluent typing and follows the logic of "if candidate is a snippet - it should be inserted". Relying on inserted word when completion menu is visible is not an intended use case, as that word can be more or less arbitrary.

> So, when I intentionally discard a completion ...

To intentionally discard completion, press `<C-e>`.

Closing as working as expected.

I understand some of your concerns, but still don't fully agree. Here’s my argument:

> Relying on inserted word when completion menu is visible is not an intended use case, as that word can be more or less arbitrary.

This is true. I just realized that the string shown in the menu can mismatch with the actual word to be inserted (most likely because of [this](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/301ee9f3afa2224b833de7c182574ba6c61e8c6e/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1253)), which I find quite counterintuitive though.

However, in many cases, since I deliberately use `<C-n>/<C-p>` to select a completion instead of `<Up>/<Down>`, I expect the selection to be inserted to help me reduce keystrokes.

> It is present for easier, more fluent typing and follows the logic of "if candidate is a snippet - it should be inserted".

This can indeed be convenient when typing functions: select a proper function and then press `(` to trigger the snippet. But another point is that when I go to select a function, my typing flow has already been broken, as I need at least one `<C-n>/<Down>` to select the first candidate.

For the two cases (first is current behavior where snippets expand anyway; second is my expected behavior where snippets expand only if accepted), the second option is more or less compatible with the first since I can deliberately choose which key triggers a snippet expansion (as shown in below video). However, for the first case, I can't find a good solution to achieve the second.

The second case is also the default behavior of Neovim's built-in completion, as well as other popular completion plugins like `blink.cmp` and `nvim-cmp`. Nevertheless, I couldn't say that the majority's choice is always the right one.

I added some configurations to the aforementioned patch to make it closer to my real use case:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4aa4dfdf-9983-4f05-ade9-5ae24332ea38

<details>

```lua
-- Remove the argument part from each function completion.
local remove_arguments = function(items)
  for _, item in ipairs(items) do
    if item.kind == vim.lsp.protocol.CompletionItemKind.Function and type(item.label) == 'string' then
      local new_label = item.label:match('^([-_.%w]+)%(.*%)')
      item.label = new_label or item.label
    end
  end
end
local process_items = function(items, base)
  remove_arguments(items)
  return MiniCompletion.default_process_items(items, base)
end
require('mini.completion').setup({
  lsp_completion = { process_items = process_items },
})

-- Press '<CR>' to expand snippet when selected
_G.cr_action = function()
  if vim.fn.complete_info()['selected'] ~= -1 then return '\25' end
  return '\r'
end
vim.keymap.set('i', '<CR>', 'v:lua.cr_action()', { expr = true })

-- Press '(' to expand snippet when selected
_G.pair_action = function()
  if vim.fn.complete_info()['selected'] ~= -1 then return '\25' end
  return '('
end
vim.keymap.set('i', '(', 'v:lua.pair_action()', { expr = true })
```

</details>

The link is [here](https://github.com/loichyan/mini.nvim/commit/5a4149d67c3f6762c281f1f91d51b794dae25183).

Anyway, whether you still hold your choice or not, there is a solution—albeit not perfect—to intentionally discard the completion while preserving the insertion:

```lua
-- Seems entering normal mode forces the popup menu to be closed.
vim.keymap.set("i", "<C-c>", "<C-o><Esc>")
```

**Update:**

> This is true. I just realized that the string shown in the menu can mismatch with the actual word to be inserted (most likely because of [this](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/301ee9f3afa2224b833de7c182574ba6c61e8c6e/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1253)), which I find quite counterintuitive though.

I found a solution that can resolve this problem:

```lua
---Removes the argument part from each function-like completion item.
local postprocess_items = function(items)
  if type(items) ~= 'table' then return items end
  for _, item in ipairs(items) do
    local word = item.abbr or item.word
    item.abbr = word -- Show the original word anyway
    item.word = word:match('([-_.%w]+)%(.*%)') or item.word
  end
  return items
end

require('mini.completion').setup()

local completefunc = MiniCompletion.completefunc_lsp
MiniCompletion.completefunc_lsp = function(...) return postprocess_items(completefunc(...)) end
```

[Link to changes](https://github.com/loichyan/mini.nvim/compare/0e9d1f972a91acf5a0513319099ba41f7c09c30a...loichyan:mini.nvim:issue/improve-funciton-completion)

This way, I can control the word that gets actually inserted. However, it feels a bit hacky to override MiniCompletion's built-in functions. Could you consider adding an option to post-process completion items? Neovim's built-in `vim.lsp.completion` supports using `convert(lsp_items): cmp_items` to achieve this ([here](https://neovim.io/doc/user/lsp.html#vim.lsp.completion.enable()) and [here](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/8d154e5927d728cc2ad74a0dec8b45fab1333f8c/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/completion.lua#L56-L59)).

btw, this solution can work even better if #1944 is resolved.

> However, in many cases, since I deliberately use `<C-n>/<C-p>` to select a completion instead of `<Up>/<Down>`, I expect the selection to be inserted to help me reduce keystrokes.

For snippet candidates it is inserted, but only its (usually) shorter version. It is in general not reasonable to have the full snippet text inserted as is because it usually leads to having explicit tabstops present (like `for ${1:i} = ${2:1}, ${3, n} do ...`). Adjusting candidate to remove those tabstops is way out of scope of 'mini.completion' (as it is very non-trivial).

> However, for the first case, I can't find a good solution to achieve the second.
> 
> The second case is also the default behavior of Neovim's built-in completion, as well as other popular completion plugins like `blink.cmp` and `nvim-cmp`. Nevertheless, I couldn't say that the majority's choice is always the right one.

Because the whole design is targeted for the user to only have to select and keep typing what was meant later to be typed. I explained it in a bit more detail [here](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/1944#issuecomment-3190929622).

> This way, I can control the word that gets actually inserted. However, it feels a bit hacky to override MiniCompletion's built-in functions. Could you consider adding an option to post-process completion items? Neovim's built-in `vim.lsp.completion` supports using `convert(lsp_items): cmp_items` to achieve this ([here](https://neovim.io/doc/user/lsp.html#vim.lsp.completion.enable()) and [here](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/8d154e5927d728cc2ad74a0dec8b45fab1333f8c/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/completion.lua#L56-L59)).

It was discussed earlier (can't find it now 😢) and I am not hugely opposed to it, but there is already a `config.lsp_completion.process_items` which *almost* does the same thing. While allowing to post-process actual built-in completion candidates means that changing the way they are computing is a breaking change, which I'd like to avoid.

So probably won't be added and I'd encourage you to go the `config.lsp_completion.process_items` route. Use [`default_process_items()`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/0b3a8b3d7811b4ac473b412251db6ea92d34fb52/doc/mini-completion.txt#L368-L376) first and then adjust entries as you see fit.

Thanks for your patience!

Though I was not fully convinced, this is not a really big problem: I myself only encountered it when inputting functions. It's not worth switching to other plugins for this issue, since mini.completion works pretty nice in 90% cases (thanks again for your thorough consideration 😊, there are many aspects I didn't take into account previously). Anyway, I have found a relatively reliable solution for my use case (and for anyone who needs similar features):

```lua
-- Resolve #1944
local process_lsp_items = function(items)
  local snippet_kind = vim.lsp.protocol.CompletionItemKind.Snippet
  local snippet_format = vim.lsp.protocol.InsertTextFormat.Snippet

  for _, item in ipairs(items) do
    -- Match only the name for completion filtering of function-like items.
    local textedit = vim.tbl_get(item, 'textEdit', 'newText')
    local inserttext = item.insertText
    local word = textedit or inserttext or item.label
    local new_word = word:match('([-_.%w]+)%(.*%)')

    if not new_word then goto continue end
    item.filterText = item.filterText or new_word

    -- Adds a tabstop anyway for functions anyway to resolve
    -- <https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/1938>.
    local is_snippet_kind = item.kind == snippet_kind
    local is_snippet_format = item.insertTextFormat == snippet_format
    if not is_snippet_kind and not is_snippet_format then goto continue end

    local has_tabstop = word:find('[^\\]%${?%w') or word:find('^%${?%w')
    if has_tabstop then
    elseif textedit then
      item.textEdit.newText = textedit .. '$0'
    else
      item.insertText = inserttext .. '$0'
    end

    ::continue::
  end

  return items
end

require('mini.completion').setup({
  lsp_completion = { process_items = process_lsp_items },
})

-- Resolve #1938
-- Completely disable the CompleteDonePre event
local enable_comp = function() vim.opt.eventignore:remove('CompleteDonePre') end
local disable_comp = function() vim.opt.eventignore:append('CompleteDonePre') end
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('InsertEnter', { callback = disable_comp })
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('InsertLeave', { callback = enable_comp })

-- But enable it for certain keys
local whitelist = { '<C-y>', '<CR>', '(' }
for _, key in ipairs(whitelist) do
  vim.keymap.set('i', key, function()
    enable_comp()
    local rawkey = vim.api.nvim_replace_termcodes(key, true, true, true)
    vim.api.nvim_feedkeys(rawkey, 'n', false)
    vim.schedule(disable_comp)
  end)
end
```

Here is the [link](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/compare/0e9d1f972a91acf5a0513319099ba41f7c09c30a...loichyan:mini.nvim:issue/improve-function-completion-v2).

> Anyway, I have found a relatively reliable solution for my use case (and for anyone who needs similar features):

This looks... complicated 👀 Couple of quick things I noticed:
- Put definitions of `snippet_kind` and `snippet_format` outside of `process_items` (for performance).
- Try to not use `goto` as it is not a Lua 5.1 feature. It just happens to be present in LuaJIT, but plugins and configs should target Lua 5.1 feature set (`:h lua-compat`).

title: [mini.completion] Should not insert snippets if reason for CompleteDone is 'discard'
